scope: Native read/ls structured output, independent from raw sandbox fs operations
implementation: read validates line/page/preview fields and returns wrapped metadata and line-numbered text/Markdown/archive previews through FileTransformer. CRLF bytes in selected lines follow the pinned source behavior.
ls validates nonnegative numeric depth, uses a typed directory manifest, includes hidden entries, preserves source tree display limits, and does not follow child directory links.

Formatted filesystem capture and transformation run in QtConcurrent jobs holding immutable roots/parameters and a shared cancellation flag. Completion is checked against request identity and generation.
Windows file contents and directory names are read through the same validated handle. Recursive directory capture uses validated canonical parent paths and validates each opened child handle.
Raw fs text/binary/list operations retain their existing separate transport. Reserved unimplemented mount prefixes cannot silently fall through to the workspace.

cases: Inclusive ranges, CRLF, preview promotion, Markdown outline, invalid type/range/depth rejection, directory depth including fractions and hidden names, budget/truncation envelope, raw binary preservation, apps without workspace, queued cancellation, reserved mount ambiguity
Deterministic junction retarget between final-path validation and enumeration; before/fixed reproduction
Held worker cancellation, same-ID replacement and destruction with protected prior object storage

limits: Tool output is currently stored inline in conversation history. The source uses compact acknowledgments and context reinjection from references; that lifecycle is a separate pending slice.
Formatted read is currently text-only transport; image/PDF/RAW/AST source transforms and formatted att/ routing remain incomplete.
The native host bounds file capture to 4 MiB, directory manifests to 10000 entries and depth 32; these are explicit native limits.
Cancellation immediately retires the result and checks the flag between bounded operations; it does not forcibly interrupt a currently blocking OS read.
Initial scope resolution still performs bounded path checks on the caller thread; this is not a claim that every filesystem operation is asynchronous.
Directory captures are not atomic filesystem-wide snapshots. POSIX branch has not been runtime-tested.
